justifications.decision: Force of atha in the sūtra
justifications.chosen: atha is a topic-opening/undertaking marker: “Now:” in the sense of opening the adhikāra.

evidence.translation: “The word atha has the sense of adhikāra.”

options_considered: the treatise/instruction on yoga as the topic
justifications.chosen: yogānuśāsanam denotes the śāstra of authoritative instruction on yoga now being undertaken.

evidence.translation: “The yogānuśāsana is to be understood as the śāstra that has been taken up as the topic.”

options_considered: union/yoking in the ordinary lexical sense
justifications.chosen: Yoga (yoga) is rendered technically as samādhi, not as generic yoking or union.

evidence.translation: “And that is a property of the mind in all its grounds.”

justifications.decision: Technical scope of samādhi/yoga after the opening sūtra
options_considered: every instance of concentration counts as yoga
only ordinary mental focusing is meant
the restricted samādhi described by Vyāsa
justifications.chosen: The yoga to be expounded is not any distracted concentration; it is the samādhi that illumines a real object, attenuates kleśas, loosens karmic bonds, turns toward nirodha, and also the asaṃprajñāta samādhi of total cessation of vṛttis.

evidence.quote: tatra vikṣipte cetasi vikṣepopasarjanībhūtaḥ samādhir na yogapakṣe vartate.
evidence.translation: “There, in a distracted mind, a samādhi subordinated to distraction does not fall within the class of yoga.”

evidence.quote: yas tv ekāgre cetasi sadbhūtam arthaṃ pradyotayati kṣiṇoti ca kleśān karmabandhanāni ślathayati nirodham abhimukhaṃ karoti sa saṃprajñāto yoga ity ākhyāyate.
evidence.translation: “But that which, in a one-pointed mind, makes a real object shine forth, destroys the kleśas, loosens the bonds of karma, and turns toward cessation is called saṃprajñāta yoga.”
“But when all vṛttis have ceased, it is asaṃprajñāta samādhi.”

translation:
At the beginning he manifests for the world’s benefit in many ways—his mass of afflictions worn away, bearing dread poison, many-mouthed, fair-coiled; source of all knowledge, with serpents for his retinue, always for its delight. May that god, the Lord of Serpents, white and stainless in body, giver of yoga, joined to yoga, protect you.

Now: the authoritative instruction on yoga (yoga, i.e. samādhi).
one_shot_delta: Without the bhāṣya, yoga in 1.1 would plausibly be translated as “union” or “yoking”; Vyāsa explicitly says yogaḥ samādhiḥ (line 3).
Without the bhāṣya, atha might be flattened to a merely temporal “then/now”; Vyāsa marks it as adhikārārtha, opening the topic (line 1).
A commentary-blind translation could miss that yogānuśāsanam is the śāstra now undertaken, not merely a loose “discipline”; line 2 states yogānuśāsanaṃ śāstram adhikṛtaṃ veditavyam.
Following the automatic tagger would misread avyāt as from √vī; the verse is a standard benediction, “may he protect you,” from √av.
A purely lexical rendering could take subhogī as “good enjoyer”; the surrounding serpent terms ahīśaḥ, bhujaga-, and anekavaktraḥ favour “fair-coiled/ringed.”
analyzer_disagreements: The tagger lemmatizes prabhavati as prabhū; following the required format, this is analyzed as bare root √bhū with prefix pra- in kartari laṭ, 3rd singular.
The tagger’s api_seg gives jagantaḥ and local_SLM uses jagant; the printed/contextual form is jagataḥ, genitive singular neuter of jagat, “of the world.”
The tagger prints/analyzes ādyaṃ in sandhi; the pausal form for the accusative singular neuter is ādyam.
The tagger splits several printed compounds into separate members; the apparatus retains the printed compounds as single inflected words and supplies samāsa analyses.
sarvajñānaprasūtiḥ was tagged masculine; it is analyzed here as feminine nominative singular from prasūti f., an appositional noun meaning “source/origin.”
yasya was tagged masculine genitive singular; the form is also neuter, and here it is construed with jagat, hence neuter genitive singular in the analysis.

vaḥ was left only as an ambiguous pronominal particle; in sa vo 'vyāt it is accusative plural, the object of “may he protect.” Because the second-person pronoun is common-gender, Pum is entered only as the formal linga value for the subanta slot.
avyāt was analyzed by the tagger under √vī; context and idiom require āśīr-liṅ of √av, “may he protect.”
The supplied local_SLM did not analyze the sūtra words atha yogānuśāsanam; they are added from the printed unit and the bhāṣya.
open_questions: The supplied bhāṣya comments on the sūtra, not on the maṅgala verse; therefore the verse’s syntax, especially yasya prītaye and adverbial ādyaṃ, is decided from grammar and context rather than commentary.
The neuter yogānuśāsanam is nominative/accusative syncretic; it is analyzed as a nominative title because the bhāṣya treats it as the śāstra being undertaken.
mula: ādyaṃ prabhavati jagato 'nekadhānugrahāya prakṣīṇakleśarāśir viṣamaviṣadharo 'nekavaktraḥ subhogī / sarvajñānaprasūtir bhujagaparikaraḥ prītaye yasya nityaṃ devo 'hīśaḥ sa vo 'vyāt sitavimalatanur yogado yogayuktaḥ //1// atha yogānuśāsanam
commentary_lines: kṣiptaṃ mūḍhaṃ vikṣiptam ekāgraṃ niruddham iti cittabhūmayaḥ.
tatra vikṣipte cetasi vikṣepopasarjanībhūtaḥ samādhir na yogapakṣe vartate.
yas tv ekāgre cetasi sadbhūtam arthaṃ pradyotayati kṣiṇoti ca kleśān karmabandhanāni ślathayati nirodham abhimukhaṃ karoti sa saṃprajñāto yoga ity ākhyāyate.
sa ca vitarkānugato vicārānugata ānandānugato 'smitānugata ity upariṣṭān nivedayiṣyāmaḥ.
